mainTopic: Hanging after execution, judging two cases in one day, a court's emergency powers, and the burial of the executed
overview: The גמרא first finishes the argument over who is hung after execution. רבנן include only the מגדף and עבודה זרה, while רבי אליעזר, reading the פסוקים as ריבוי ומיעוט, includes all the נסקלין. Next it explains why רבנן do not hang a woman ('באיש', not a woman). It also shows how רבי אליעזר uses the extra words: 'אותו' teaches that the body is hung without clothing, and the double exclusion in 'באיש חטא' includes the בן סורר ומורה. Then the גמרא explains the rule that a court does not judge two capital cases on one day. רב חסדא's view is reworded so that it allows this only for the same death penalty and the same sin. A ברייתא then teaches that a בית דין may punish beyond the תורה when the times demand it, with two stories as examples. A new משנה describes how the body is hung and that it must be taken down right away. It explains 'קללת אלהים', and רבי מאיר teaches that God feels pain even over the wicked. The משנה ends with the burial rules and with the relatives making peace with the דיינים and the עדים.

steps.title: רבנן's reading: distance between the phrases adds idol worship
steps.stepSummary: Because the כלל and the פרט are far apart, the פסוקים include עבודה זרה, which is like the מגדף in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the general phrase and the specific phrase are far from each other, they work to include an idol worshipper, who is similar to the blasphemer in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבנן's explanation of why, besides the מגדף, an idol worshipper is also hung after execution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כלל and פרט were close together, only the מגדף would be included. Because they are written far apart, the inclusion widens a little. It reaches עבודה זרה, which matches the מגדף in every way, but no further.

keyTerms.meaning: they are far from each other
it is effective, it accomplishes something

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבנן limit hanging to exactly two people: the מגדף and the idol worshipper.

phrases.english: Now that they are distant from each other,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the general phrase and the specific phrase from the פסוקים discussed just before.

phrases.english: they serve to include idol worship,
which is similar to it in all matters.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the blasphemer, the case the פסוק is mainly talking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבנן's derivation, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבנן, the far-apart כלל and פרט include עבודה זרה together with the מגדף.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reading: all who are stoned are hung
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the same פסוקים as ריבוי ומיעוט, and because the phrases are far apart, all the נסקלין are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר learns using 'inclusions and exclusions.' 'And he is put to death, and you shall hang' is an inclusion. 'For a curse' is an exclusion. If they were next to each other, we would include only idol worship, which is like the blasphemer in everything. Since they are far apart, they include all the others who are stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי אליעזר reaches his wider ruling from the same פסוקים, using a different method of reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן's method, כלל ופרט, starts narrow. רבי אליעזר's method, ריבוי ומיעוט, starts wide. In both methods the distance between the phrases widens the result. For רבי אליעזר, that means every person executed by stoning is hung.

keyTerms.meaning: inclusions and exclusions, a method of reading the תורה
the rest of those who are stoned

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides say 'now that they are far apart, include more.' The results differ because they start from different methods: כלל ופרט for רבנן, ריבוי ומיעוט for רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: only the מגדף and עבודה זרה are hung. רבי אליעזר: all the נסקלין are hung.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer interprets by inclusions and exclusions:
"And he is put to death, and you shall hang" is an inclusion,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: "For a curse of" is an exclusion.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:23. The פסוק speaks of the blasphemer, who curses God, so it narrows things down to him.

phrases.english: If they were close to each other,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ מְרַבִּינַן אֶלָּא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: we would include only idol worship,
which is similar to it in all matters.
Now that they are distant from each other,
they serve to include the rest of those who are stoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אליעזר's parallel derivation from the same פסוקים, using a different method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, all who are executed by stoning are hung.

steps.title: Why do רבנן say a woman is not hung?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about hanging a man and asks for רבנן's source that a woman is not hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A man is hung, etc.' What is the reason of רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next argument in the משנה and asks where רבנן get the rule that a woman is not hung. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר holds that a woman is also hung, facing the tree. רבנן say only a man is hung. The גמרא wants the פסוק behind רבנן's view.

phrases.english: "A man is hung, etc."
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: hanging a woman.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבנן's rule that a woman is not hung.

steps.title: 'Him' and not 'her'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'hang him,' which teaches that a woman is not hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and you shall hang him.' Him, not her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to the word 'אותו' (him) in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'and you shall hang.' Since it adds the masculine word 'him,' רבנן read it as leaving out a woman.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And you shall hang him"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: him, and not her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אותו' (him) leaves out a woman.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר uses 'him' for something else
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'אותו' as teaching that the man is hung without his clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He says 'him' means him alone, without his clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר is not bothered by the word 'him': he uses it to teach a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אותו' clearly left out a woman, רבי אליעזר's view would be hard to hold. So he gives the word a different job: the body is hung bare, without clothing. That leaves no extra word to exclude a woman.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking, without spelling it out, what רבי אליעזר does with the word 'him.'

phrases.english: "Him" means without his clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אליעזר deals with the word that רבנן used as their source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' seems to clearly exclude a woman, which would go against רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר, 'אותו' teaches that the man is hung without clothing, not that a woman is left out.

steps.title: רבנן agree, but learn from 'a man'
steps.stepSummary: רבנן agree that 'אותו' means without clothing. They learn that a woman is not hung from the word 'באיש' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? Yes, they agree that 'him' means without clothing. But their source is the פסוק 'And if there is in a man a sin': a man, and not a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבנן learn the 'without clothing' rule. It answers that they accept that reading of 'אותו' and take their source for 'not a woman' from another word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'אותו' is used for 'without clothing,' רבנן need a new source to exclude a woman. They find it in the word 'באיש' (in a man). So both sides agree on 'without clothing.' The argument is only over whether 'באיש' leaves out a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: a man, and not a woman

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree the body is hung without clothing (from 'אותו'). רבנן exclude a woman because the פסוק says 'באיש.'

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Meaning: where do the Rabbis learn that he is hung without his clothing?

phrases.aramaic: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי. אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so. But the verse states:
"And if there is in a man a sin"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: a man, and not a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to רבנן after step 5: where do they learn 'without clothing'? They agree it comes from 'אותו', so they must take 'not a woman' from 'באיש' instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreement on one reading plus a new source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן seemed to need 'אותו' to exclude a woman, which would leave them no source for 'without clothing.'
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן use 'אותו' for 'without clothing' and 'באיש' to exclude a woman.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'באיש'?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי אליעזר does not use ״באיש״ to exclude women, the גמרא asks what he does learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר: what does he learn from the words 'And if there be in a man'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said that רבנן learn from ״באיש״ that a woman is not hung. Now it asks what רבי אליעזר, who does hang women, does with that same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule that no word in the תורה is extra. If רבי אליעזר does not use ״באיש״ to exclude women, he must use it to teach something else, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?
'And if there be in a man': the opening words of the פסוק about hanging

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
this phrase, 'And if there be in a man',
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי ״וְכִי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ״ מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question back on רבי אליעזר after רבנן's use of ״באיש״ was explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from the word ״באיש״.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it excludes the rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that ״באיש״ excludes a בן סורר ומורה from being hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: That word comes to exclude a stubborn and rebellious son.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives an answer: for רבי אליעזר, ״באיש״ means a grown man, so a בן סורר ומורה, who is a boy, is not hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'man' is now read as excluding a child instead of a woman. A בן סורר ומורה is a young boy, so on this reading he would be stoned but not hung.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
That comes to exclude a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָהוּא לְמַעוֹטֵי בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״באיש״ excludes the בן סורר ומורה from hanging.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי אליעזר does hang the rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying the בן סורר ומורה is stoned and then hung, which contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: A stubborn and rebellious son is stoned and hung. These are the words of רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר himself says the בן סורר ומורה IS hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said that according to רבי אליעזר the word excludes the son from hanging. The ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר holds the opposite, so ריש לקיש's explanation cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא), used to bring a challenge

phrases.english: But it was taught:
a stubborn and rebellious son is stoned and hung,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה נִסְקָל וְנִתְלֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי אליעזר excludes the בן סורר ומורה from hanging.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר ruling the exact opposite.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: it includes the rebellious son
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק replaces ריש לקיש's answer: for רבי אליעזר, the words come to include the בן סורר ומורה in hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It comes to include a stubborn and rebellious son.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the ברייתא, the גמרא gives a new answer: the phrase teaches that the בן סורר ומורה IS hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is now the reverse of ריש לקיש's: 'include' instead of 'exclude'. This fits the ברייתא, but it raises an obvious question, since a phrase about 'a man' seems to leave out a boy. The next step explains how.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and gives a new one)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It comes to include a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לְרַבּוֹת בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's answer, which the ברייתא knocked down.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר, the phrase includes the בן סורר ומורה in hanging.

steps.title: Two exclusions in a row include
steps.stepSummary: ״איש״ excludes a boy, and ״חטא״ excludes someone killed for his future. Two exclusions in a row teach inclusion, so the בן סורר ומורה is hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says 'And if there be in a man a sin.' 'Man' means not a son. 'Sin' means someone killed for a sin he did, which leaves out the בן סורר ומורה, who is killed because of what he will become. That is an exclusion after an exclusion, and an exclusion after an exclusion only comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how 'man' can include a boy, then explains with a rule of reading the תורה: two exclusions of the same thing, one after another, actually mean that thing is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״איש״ alone would leave out the boy. ״חטא״ would leave him out a second time, because he is killed for the future and not for a sin already done. Saying the same exclusion twice is treated as a sign of inclusion, so the בן סורר ומורה is hung.

keyTerms.meaning: because of what he will end up doing
an exclusion after an exclusion, which teaches inclusion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think two exclusions make the exclusion stronger. In this rule, the second exclusion cancels the first, so the result is to include.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
As the verse says: 'And if there be in a man a sin'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: – 'a man,' and not a son.
'A sin': one who is killed for his sin,
which leaves out the stubborn and rebellious son,
who is killed because of his end.
phrases.notes: He hasn't done anything deserving death yet. He is killed now because of where he is heading.

phrases.english: So it is an exclusion after an exclusion,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and an exclusion after an exclusion comes only to include.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכִי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ חֵטְא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״איש״ and ״חטא״ are two exclusions of the בן סורר ומורה, and two exclusions in a row include him.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, ״באיש חטא״ is an exclusion after an exclusion, so the בן סורר ומורה is stoned AND hung.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: שמעון בן שטח hung women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in which רבי אליעזר brings proof from שמעון בן שטח, who hung women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: Didn't שמעון בן שטח hang women, etc.?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This is a setup line, and the next step comments on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר brought proof that women are hung. The רבנן answered that שמעון בן שטח hung eighty women in one day, which normally is not allowed, so it was an emergency step and proves nothing. The גמרא is about to explain that rule about one day.

keyTerms.meaning: An early leader who hung women for witchcraft in Ashkelon
etc.: the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח תָּלָה נָשִׁים כּוּ׳?
phrases.english: Didn't Shimon ben Shatach hang women, etc.?
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: the רבנן answered that he hung eighty women in one day, and two people are not judged on one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וַהֲלֹא שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח תָּלָה נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's proof from שמעון בן שטח, and the רבנן's answer about judging two people in one day.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the rule is only about two kinds of death
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that the ban on judging two people in one day applies only when they get two different death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They only taught this about two kinds of death. But with one kind of death, the court may judge them on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא limits the rule from the משנה that a court does not judge two capital cases on one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to him, the ban applies only if the two cases need different death penalties, for example one stoning and one burning. If both get the same death penalty, the court may judge both on one day.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when...: limits a rule

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They only taught this about two kinds of death,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that a court does not judge two capital cases on one day.

phrases.english: but with one kind of death, they may judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the rule that the רבנן used in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two capital cases may not be judged on one day only if they involve two different death penalties.

steps.title: But שמעון בן שטח's case was one kind of death
steps.stepSummary: All the women of שמעון בן שטח got the same death penalty, yet the רבנן said that should not be done, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the story of שמעון בן שטח involved one kind of death, and yet they told him the court may not judge them on one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the very story in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the women got the same death penalty. Even so, the רבנן said it is not normally allowed to judge them on one day. So the ban must also apply to cases with one death penalty, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: But the story (used to bring a challenge)

phrases.english: But the story of Shimon ben Shatach
was one kind of death,
and yet they said about it that we may not judge!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּשִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח דְּמִיתָה אַחַת הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's limit on the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that one death penalty may be judged on one day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמעון בן שטח's case had one death penalty, and the רבנן still said it is not allowed.

steps.title: Restated: one death penalty but two different sins
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's statement is reworded: the ban covers one death penalty for two different sins. Only one death penalty for one sin may be judged on one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: They only taught this about one kind of death that is like two kinds of death. What case is that? For example, two different sins. But with one kind of death and one sin, the court may judge on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords רב חסדא's statement so that it fits the story of שמעון בן שטח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban now also applies to the same death penalty if it comes for two different sins, since that is like two separate cases. That fits שמעון בן שטח's women, who got one death penalty but for different sins. Only when it is the same death penalty for the same sin may the court judge them on one day.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said: correcting how a statement was reported

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רב חסדא: two capital cases may be judged on one day only if they share the same death penalty AND the same sin.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמִיתָה אַחַת כְּעֵין שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת.
phrases.english: They only taught this about one kind of death that is like two kinds of death.
And what case is that?
For example, two different sins.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּמִיתָה אַחַת וַעֲבֵירָה אַחַת – דָּנִין.
phrases.english: But with one kind of death and one sin, they may judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אִיתְּמַר הָכִי אִיתְּמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמִיתָה אַחַת כְּעֵין שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes רב חסדא's statement in answer to the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording how the statement was reported
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only two different death penalties are banned on one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even one death penalty for two different sins is banned. Only one death penalty for one sin is allowed.

steps.title: Even an adulterer and adulteress may not be judged on one day
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes a ברייתא: two people may not be judged on one day, not even an adulterer and an adulteress. This seems to go against רב חסדא, since they did the same sin and get the same death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה challenged: We do not judge two people on one day, not even an adulterer and an adulteress.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks רב חסדא's rule from step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said only cases of the same death penalty for the same sin may be judged on one day. A man and woman who committed adultery together did one sin and normally get the same death. Yet the ברייתא says even they may not be judged on one day, which contradicts רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava raises an objection:
We do not judge two people on one day,
not even an adulterer and an adulteress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reworded rule of רב חסדא from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that one death penalty for one sin may be judged on one day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The adulterer and adulteress share one sin and one penalty, yet the ברייתא forbids judging them on one day.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about cases with two different death penalties
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a כהן's daughter and the man with her, or a כהן's daughter and certain false witnesses. In both cases the two people get different death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it as talking about a כהן's daughter and the man who was with her, or a כהן's daughter and the false witnesses who tried to discredit her witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends his rule by showing the ברייתא is talking about a special case where the penalties differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת כהן who sins this way gets שריפה (burning), while the man with her gets a different death. So even though it is one act, there are two different penalties, which fits רב חסדא's rule. He gives a second example with false witnesses who also get a different death than she does.

keyTerms.meaning: he explained it (gave it a new reading)
the man who was with her
witnesses proven to be false plotters

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is a normal adulterer and adulteress. רב חסדא picks a case where the woman's punishment is different from the man's, which is why judging them together is banned.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda explained it:
as talking about a כהן's daughter and the man who was with her,
phrases.notes: She gets burning, while he gets a different death, so it's two penalties.

phrases.english: or a כהן's daughter and the false witnesses who tried to discredit her witnesses.
phrases.notes: Here too, she is burned and those witnesses get a different death, so again two different penalties.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא speaks of an ordinary adulterer and adulteress with the same penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a בת כהן with a partner or witnesses who get a different death penalty, so it fits רב חסדא.

steps.title: A court may punish beyond the תורה to protect the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he heard that a בית דין may whip and punish even where the תורה does not require it. This is not to go against the תורה, but to build a fence around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: I heard that a court may whip and punish even when the תורה does not require it, not to go against the תורה, but to make a fence around the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the special power of a בית דין to give punishments the תורה does not call for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a court gives only the punishments the תורה sets. Here we learn that in special situations a court may punish more, as a protective step. The goal is to keep people from breaking the תורה, not to change the תורה's laws.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
a fence around the Torah, a protective step

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the idea that a בית דין can make emergency rulings (הוראת שעה) to protect תורה observance.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
I heard that a court may whip and punish
even when it is not from the Torah,
and not in order to go against the words of the Torah,
but in order to make a fence around the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the court's emergency powers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין may punish beyond Torah law as a protective fence, not to override the Torah.

steps.title: The man who rode a horse on שבת was stoned
steps.stepSummary: In the days of the Greeks, a man rode a horse on שבת and the court stoned him. He did not really deserve it, but the times called for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story of a man who rode a horse on שבת in the days of the Greeks. They brought him to court and stoned him, not because he deserved it, but because the times needed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a real story that shows the rule of step 18 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding a horse on שבת does not carry the death penalty from the תורה. Still, the court stoned him because people were becoming careless about שבת. This shows that a court may give a harsh punishment as an emergency step.

keyTerms.meaning: a story, an incident that happened
the times needed it, an emergency measure

phrases.english: And there was a story with someone who rode a horse
on שבת in the days of the Greeks,
and they brought him to court and stoned him,
not because he deserved it,
phrases.notes: Riding a horse on שבת is only a rabbinic ban, so the תורה doesn't give death for it.

phrases.english: but because the times needed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁרָכַב עַל סוּס בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב with a story.
steps.raayaObject: A court may punish beyond Torah law when the times require it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man stoned for riding a horse on שבת in Greek times.

steps.title: The man who was with his wife under a fig tree was whipped
steps.stepSummary: A man was with his wife in public under a fig tree, and the court gave him lashes. He did not really deserve it, but the times called for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another story: a man was with his wife under a fig tree. They brought him to court and gave him lashes, not because he deserved it, but because the times needed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second story showing the same emergency power of the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being with one's own wife is not a crime in the תורה, so lashes are not normally due. The court still whipped him because modesty had fallen apart. Together with the horse story, it shows the court can punish for the sake of the times.
steps.whatToRemember: A בית דין may give punishments beyond the תורה, even death or lashes, when the times require it, to build a fence around the תורה, never to override it.

phrases.english: Another story with a certain man
who was with his wife under the fig tree,
phrases.notes: He means out in the open, where people could see.

phrases.english: and they brought him to court and gave him lashes,
not because he deserved it,
but because the times needed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהֵטִיחַ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ תַּחַת הַתְּאֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story supporting the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: A court may give lashes beyond Torah law when the times require it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man whipped for being with his wife under a fig tree.

steps.title: How the stoned man's body is hung
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first opinion about how the body of a stoned person is hung: a post is sunk into the ground with a crossbar, and the body is hung by its tied hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do they hang him? They sink a post into the ground with a piece of wood sticking out. He puts the man's two hands one on top of the other and hangs him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains exactly how the body of someone executed by סקילה is hung after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that certain people who are stoned are also hung afterward. Now the משנה describes the method: an upright post in the ground, a crossbar sticking out, and the body hung by its tied hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of a new משנה
They sink something in or plant it firmly

steps.confusionAlert: The hanging happens only after the person is already dead. It is not a way of killing him.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How do they hang him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the body of the person who was stoned, from the previous משנה.

phrases.english: They sink the post into the ground,
and a piece of wood sticks out from it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַקִּיף שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: and he puts his two hands together, one on top of the other,
and hangs him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of a court punishing beyond the letter of the law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The body is hung from a crossbar on a post sunk in the ground, by its two tied hands.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the post leans on a wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the post is not sunk into the ground. It leans against a wall, and the body is hung the way butchers hang meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: The post leans against the wall, and he hangs him the way butchers do.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees about the method. In his view the post leans against a wall instead of being planted in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions agree that the body is hung. They argue only about how the hanging structure is set up. רבי יוסי compares it to the way butchers hang meat on a pole propped against a wall.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
The post leans against the wall,
and he hangs him
the way that butchers do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion on the method described in step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The post leans against a wall, and the body is hung like butchered meat.

steps.title: The body must be taken down right away
steps.stepSummary: The body is untied right away. Leaving it hanging overnight breaks a לא תעשה, from the פסוק 'לא תלין נבלתו על העץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They untie him right away. If he stays hanging overnight, one transgresses a לא תעשה, as it says: 'His body shall not remain all night on the tree, but you shall surely bury him, for a hanged one is a curse of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says how long the body stays up: only a moment. It brings a פסוק to show that leaving it overnight is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hanging is very brief. The פסוק forbids leaving the body up overnight and commands burying it. The last part of the פסוק, 'כי קללת אלהים תלוי', is the source the משנה explains in the next steps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is also the source for the wider rule in step 27, that no dead person may be left unburied overnight.

phrases.english: And they untie him right away,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָן – עוֹבֵר עָלָיו בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: and if he stays overnight, one transgresses a prohibition because of him,
as it says:
"His body shall not remain all night on the tree,
but you shall surely bury him,
for a hanged one is a curse of God, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the hanging rules by saying how long the body may stay up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The body is taken down right away. Leaving it overnight breaks a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Why a hanging body disgraces God's Name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains 'קללת אלהים תלוי': people will ask why this man is hanging. The answer is that he cursed God, and so God's Name is disgraced.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is to say: why is this one hanging? Because he 'blessed' God. And so it turns out that the Name of Heaven is disgraced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the reason in the פסוק. A body left hanging keeps reminding people of the curse against God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reads 'קללת אלהים' as 'a reminder of cursing God'. Anyone passing by would ask why the man is hanging, and the answer itself would mention the curse. That is a חילול השם, so the body must come down quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: That he 'blessed' God; a polite way of saying he cursed God

steps.confusionAlert: 'בירך' here does not mean he truly blessed God. It is a polite word used so the משנה does not have to say 'cursed God' directly.

phrases.english: That is to say: why is this one hanging?
Because he "blessed" God,
and it turns out that the Name of Heaven is disgraced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last words of the פסוק quoted in step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the body hanging causes חילול השם, because it reminds everyone of the curse against God.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the שכינה feels the pain
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'קללת' as 'קלני', meaning 'I am in pain'. When a person suffers, the שכינה says, 'My head is in pain, My arm is in pain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: When a person suffers, what does the שכינה say? 'I am in pain from My head, I am in pain from My arm.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a different reading of 'קללת אלהים'. He reads it as God Himself feeling pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'a curse against God', רבי מאיר links the word קללת to קלני, 'I feel heavy or pained'. So the hanging body is a source of pain to God, and that is why it must not stay up.

keyTerms.meaning: I am in pain (literally, 'it is heavy on me')

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
When a person suffers,
what expression does the Divine Presence say?
"I am in pain from My head, I am in pain from My arm."
phrases.notes: He is playing on the word קללת in the פסוק, reading it like קלני, 'I am in pain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of 'קללת אלהים' than step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'קללת אלהים' means that God feels pain when a person suffers his punishment.

steps.title: All the more so for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: From רבי מאיר's reading comes a קל וחומר: if God feels pain over the spilled blood of the wicked, He surely feels pain over the blood of צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If God suffers over the spilled blood of wicked people, all the more so over the blood of righteous people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר draws a lesson from his own reading, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The executed man deserved his punishment, yet God still feels pain over him. So when a צדיק suffers or is killed, God's pain is surely even greater.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: God feels pain even when a wicked person is rightly punished. How much more so when a צדיק suffers.

phrases.english: If God suffers like this
over the blood of the wicked that is spilled,

phrases.aramaic: קַל וְחוֹמֶר עַל דָּמָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים.
phrases.english: all the more so over the blood of the righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a קל וחומר from רבי מאיר's reading in step 25
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: God feels pain over the blood of the wicked, and all the more so over the blood of צדיקים.

steps.title: No dead person may be left unburied overnight
steps.stepSummary: The rule is not only for an executed man. Anyone who leaves any dead relative unburied overnight transgresses a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they did not say only this. Rather, anyone who leaves his dead one overnight transgresses a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the rule from the executed man to every dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was said about a hanged criminal, but the prohibition applies to every dead person. Burying on the same day applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: One who leaves a body overnight

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a dead person should be buried quickly, without delaying overnight.

phrases.english: And they did not say only this,
but anyone who leaves his dead one overnight
transgresses a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the prohibition from step 23 to every dead person
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving any dead person unburied overnight breaks a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Exception: a delay for the dead person's honor
steps.stepSummary: If the burial is delayed overnight for the dead person's honor, such as bringing a coffin and shrouds, there is no transgression.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he left him overnight for his honor, to bring him a coffin and shrouds, he does not transgress.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to the rule it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is about disrespect to the dead. A delay that serves the dead person's honor, such as getting a proper coffin and shrouds, is not a transgression. The rule still applies; this kind of delay is simply allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Bury the dead the same day. A delay is allowed only when it is for the dead person's honor, like getting a coffin and shrouds.

phrases.english: If he left him overnight for his honor,
to bring him a coffin and shrouds,
he does not transgress because of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the general rule of step 27 with an exception
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A delay overnight for the dead person's honor does not break the prohibition.

steps.title: Two special graveyards for those executed by the court
steps.stepSummary: An executed person is not buried with his ancestors. The בית דין keeps two graveyards: one for those killed by the sword or strangled, and one for those stoned or burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would not bury him in his family's graves. Instead, the court had two graveyards ready: one for those killed by the sword or by strangling, and one for those stoned or burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the burial rules from the last steps and tells us where the executed person is buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 27-28 taught that he must be buried the same day. Now we learn the place: a separate court graveyard, not the family plot. The four death penalties are split into two pairs, with סקילה and שריפה in one graveyard and הרג and חנק in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: His ancestors' graves, the family burial plot
Those executed by stoning and by burning

phrases.english: And they would not bury him
in the graves of his ancestors,
rather, two graveyards
were set up for the court:
one for those killed by the sword and those strangled,
and one for those stoned and those burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּקִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the burial rules: after teaching that he must be buried, the משנה says where.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An executed person is buried in one of two court graveyards, grouped by type of death, and not in his family plot.

steps.title: Moving the bones to the family plot
steps.stepSummary: Once the flesh has decomposed, the bones are gathered and buried in their proper place, which is the family plot.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the flesh had decomposed, they gathered the bones and buried them in their proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains that the court graveyard is only a temporary stop. Later the bones go home to the family graves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 kept him out of his family plot. That rule only lasts until the flesh has decomposed. After that, his bones are gathered and buried with his ancestors.
steps.confusionAlert: "בִּמְקוֹמָן" does not mean the bones stay where they are in the court graveyard. It means they are moved to their proper place, the family's graves.

phrases.english: Once the flesh had decomposed,
they gather the bones
and bury them in their proper place.
phrases.notes: "Their proper place" means the family graves, the same ones he was kept out of at first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits Step 29: the separate graveyard is only until the flesh has decomposed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the flesh decomposes, the bones are moved and buried in the family plot.

steps.title: The relatives show they hold no grudge
steps.stepSummary: The relatives come and greet the דיינים and the עדים. This shows they have no hard feelings, because the judgment was true.
steps.simpleTranslation: The relatives come and ask how the judges and the witnesses are doing. They mean: we have nothing against you, because you judged a true judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by describing how the family of the executed person treats the people who judged and testified against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking after someone's welfare is a gesture of friendship. The relatives use it to show they accept the verdict and hold no anger toward the דיינים or the עדים. The reason they give is that the judgment was true.

keyTerms.meaning: They ask about someone's welfare, they greet warmly

steps.whatToRemember: The executed person is buried the same day, at first in a court graveyard. His bones later go to the family plot. His relatives make peace with the דיינים and the עדים, because the judgment was true.

phrases.english: And the relatives come and ask
about the welfare of the judges and the welfare of the witnesses,
as if to say: we hold nothing in our hearts against you,
for you judged a true judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the burial rules, the משנה closes with how the family behaves toward the court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The relatives greet the דיינים and the עדים to show they accept the true judgment and hold no grudge.
